title: Coefficient bound by absolute mean
statement: Let $n\in\mathbb N$, let $p$ assign a real coefficient $p(S)$ to each subset $S\subseteq[n]$, and let $P(x)=\sum_{T\subseteq[n]}p(T)\chi_T(x)$ be its Walsh expansion. For every $S\subseteq[n]$, \[|p(S)|\le\mathbb E_x|P(x)|,\] where the expectation is uniform on the Boolean cube.
hypotheses_covered: $p$ is a real coefficient family indexed by subsets of $[n]$
replaced: Let $n\ge0$ and equip $\{0,1\}^n$ with its uniform probability measure; write $\mathbb E$ for uniform expectation. For $S\subseteq[n]$, put $\chi_S(x)=\prod_{i\in S}(-1)^{x_i}$ and $\widehat h(S)=\mathbb E[h\chi_S]$ for real cube functions $h$. Let $P(x)=\sum_{S\subseteq[n]}a_S\chi_S(x)$ with real coefficients $a_S$. For every $S\subseteq[n]$, $|a_S|\le\mathbb E|P|$.
